case_title: Arun Raj v. Union of India and Ors.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.69 of Army Act
aggravating_circumstances: Deliberate planning, use of a sharp weapon, striking a vital part of the body
trial_court_outcome: Guilty of murder, sentenced to 7 years imprisonment and dismissed from service
neutral_facts: The accused, an army official, was charged with the murder of his colleague. According to the prosecution, the accused reported to his superior officer that the deceased and another individual had abused him. After making the complaint, the accused went to the barrack with a kitchen knife concealed in his lungi and stabbed the deceased on the right side of his chest while the deceased was sleeping. The eyewitness to the incident was present and witnessed the stabbing. The deceased succumbed to the injuries. The accused was initially sentenced to 7 years of rigorous imprisonment and dismissed from service. The sentence was later revised to life imprisonment and dismissal from service. The accused challenged the conviction and sentence, arguing that the incident was due to grave and sudden provocation and that the offense fell under Section 304 (Part II) of the IPC. The High Court rejected these arguments, finding that the accused had sufficient time to deliberate and plan the attack, and that the use of a sharp weapon on a vital part of the body indicated an intention to cause death.
